Incorporating SLOOS insights, the March 15, 2020 FOMC statement’s outlook skews more negative than the text alone suggests. SLOOS indicates banks had already tightened C&I and construction/land development standards and other loan terms across firm sizes; raised credit score thresholds and tightened credit limits; and saw weaker demand for consumer and CRE credit. Banks reported reduced risk tolerance and expected further tightening for risky loans, alongside expected deterioration in loan portfolios, collateral values, HELOCs, and performance for small-firm and syndicated loans. While the Fed’s move to the ELB, large-scale Treasury/MBS purchases, expanded repo, and swap lines support market functioning and liquidity, SLOOS points to concurrent supply- and demand-side credit headwinds that will weigh on activity and amplify downside risks in the near term. Net: more negative, partially mitigated by policy support and bank capital/liquidity strength.
